findings.title: Credential-like literal in source
findings.explanation: A credential-related name is assigned a literal or compared with one. Quoted assignments and comparisons include C and C++ character-prefixed string literals. Plain values are also checked in .env files. FUSE cannot determine whether the value is valid or used.
findings.potential_impact: If the value is an active credential and the code or firmware is distributed, an unauthorized party may recover it and access the associated service or device.
findings.remediation: Remove the literal, rotate the value if it was exposed, and provision secrets through a deployment-specific secret store or protected device provisioning flow.

findings.title: TLS peer verification appears disabled
findings.explanation: The source contains an explicit setting or API commonly used to bypass TLS certificate or hostname verification. FUSE does not establish that this path runs.
findings.potential_impact: If used for a network connection, disabling verification can allow an active attacker to impersonate the peer and intercept or alter traffic.
findings.remediation: Enable certificate-chain and hostname verification, install the correct trust anchor, and use a test-only override that cannot enter production builds.
